item.name: Authentication
item.description: Login, refresh, logout, and PKI wallet bind.

item.name: Authenticate client credentials and obtain access + refresh tokens

request.name: Authenticate client credentials and obtain access + refresh tokens

description.content:
Two authentication flows depending on the participant role:
**Direct login** (ROLE_GOVERNANCE, ROLE_SUPERVISOR, ROLE_NOC, etc.): Returns accessToken + optional refreshToken in the JSON body. Also sets HttpOnly cookies access_token and refresh_token automatically.
**PKI nonce flow** (ROLE_COMMERCIAL_BANK, ROLE_TREASURY): Returns { "nonce": "<hex>" } only — no tokens, no cookies. The client must sign the nonce and complete login via POST /auth/wallet/bind.

response.name: Login successful. For direct flows the response body contains tokens and the Set-Cookie headers inject HttpOnly cookies. For PKI flows only a nonce is returned (no cookies).

item.name: PKI re-login after onboarding (Commercial Bank proxy mode)

request.name: PKI re-login after onboarding (Commercial Bank proxy mode)

description.content:
Available only on Commercial Bank gateways with a proxy handler. Reads the saved participant certificate from `PKI_DIR/{bankCode}-participant.crt`, then executes the two-step PKI login against the Central Bank: 1. POST /auth/login with user_id + client_secret → nonce 2. Sign nonce with P-256 key → POST /auth/wallet/bind → accessToken
Returns the access token on success. Requires the participant to have completed onboarding (POST /onboarding/complete) so the certificate is on disk.

item.name: Onboarding
item.description:
3-phase PKI + Blockchain participant onboarding.
**Central Bank mode** (public endpoints at /api/v1/onboarding/): Phase 1: Commercial bank submits CSR + blockchain public key. Phase 2.5: Poll for KYC approval and PoP nonce. Phase 3: Sign PoP nonce to prove wallet ownership, receive certificate and clientSecret. Recovery: GET /api/v1/onboarding/my-status — look up status from the JWT session (BankID claim); no request_id or query parameters needed.
**Commercial Bank proxy mode** (protected endpoints at /api/v1/onboarding/): The commercial bank gateway proxies requests to the Central Bank. In smart mode (KMS + PKI configured), the proxy injects CSR, blockchain key, and PoP signature automatically — the frontend only sends metadata. GET /api/v1/onboarding/my-status with cookie — the proxy resolves the bank identity from the JWT BankID claim; the frontend sends no parameters.

The Central Bank's identity service creates a Keycloak user and stores the credential request. Poll GET /api/v1/onboarding/status/{requestId} until KYC is approved.

item.name: Recover onboarding status from JWT session (no parameters needed)

request.name: Recover onboarding status from JWT session (no parameters needed)

description.content:
**Commercial Bank mode (primary use case)** — requires `access_token` cookie.
The frontend simply calls `GET /onboarding/my-status` with the session cookie. The backend resolves the bank identity from the JWT `BankID` claim (enriched during token validation from the compliance participant record) and proxies the lookup to the Central Bank. No query parameters are needed.
**Central Bank mode** — public endpoint that accepts `bank_code` as a query parameter. Used internally by the proxy and by the governance portal when looking up a specific bank.
If `bank_code` is omitted on the Central Bank, the handler falls back to the JWT `BankID` claim (if the caller is authenticated).
Returns `request_id`, `user_id`, and `status`. Sensitive fields such as `wallet_address` and `pop_nonce` are intentionally omitted from this recovery endpoint.

Optional. Only required when calling the Central Bank endpoint directly (e.g. governance portal). On the Commercial Bank proxy, the bank identity is resolved from the JWT session — omit this parameter entirely.

item.name: Sign a PKCS#10 CSR submitted by the participant (preferred flow)

request.name: Sign a PKCS#10 CSR submitted by the participant (preferred flow)

description.content:
The participant generates their own ECDSA-P256 key pair locally, creates a PKCS#10 CSR, and delivers it to the Central Bank out-of-band. The Central Bank submits the CSR via this endpoint; the CA signs the certificate without ever seeing the participant's private key. The participant is registered with status PENDING until KYC approval (POST /api/v1/compliance/approve-kyc).
Prerequisite: the participant's Keycloak user must already exist (created via POST /api/v1/compliance/register). The user_id in the payload is the UUID returned by that endpoint.

item.name: Escrow

info.name: CBWeb3 API Gateway — Scenario B — International Hub

description.content:
OpenAPI specification for the CBWeb3 platform API Gateway (Scenario B — International Hub). Implements authentication, participant onboarding, KYC/AML compliance, governance operations over the identity service (Keycloak + KMS), and payment orchestrator operations (HTLC dual-layer + Zeto token management via Paladin sidecar + escrow deposit/tokenization/ redeem lifecycle) under the **/api/v1** core surface, plus the **/api/v2** Hub-and-Spoke AMM surface: exact-output and cross-currency swaps, lock-mint / burn-unlock bridging, cooperative + sovereign liquidity provisioning (commit-reveal), hub currency and AMM pair registries, the asymmetric circuit breaker (1-of-N pause / 2-of-N resume), and the Master Viewing Key oversight (disclosure quorum).
Security note: All /compliance and /governance write endpoints require the appropriate Central Bank / governance role. Payment endpoints (HTLC + Token) are only available when the payment orchestrator service is configured. The /api/v2 routes are registered only when their backing services are wired (per-gateway dependency injection), so a given gateway deployment may expose a subset of the v2 surface depending on its role (commercial bank vs. central bank).
